n: Second Nephi opens with Lehi’s final counsel to his family. Nephi introduces it: after Nephi taught his brothers, the aging Lehi recounted the great things God had done in bringing them out of Jerusalem.
Lehi reminds them of their rebellion on the ship and God’s mercy in sparing their lives during the storm.
He speaks of the promised land and of the Lord’s mercy in warning them to flee Jerusalem.

f.w: warning us that we should flee

n: Lehi has seen in vision that Jerusalem has been destroyed. Had they stayed, they would have died. Babylon destroyed the city in 587/586 BC.
Despite their trials, they have received a land “choice above all other lands,” covenanted to Lehi’s descendants forever and to all whom the Lord leads there from other countries.
Lehi prophesies that no one will come to this land unless the Lord brings them. Its settlement is under God’s hand.

f.w: brought by the hand of the Lord

n: The land is dedicated to those God brings. If they keep His commandments it will be a land of liberty and they will never be enslaved; but if wickedness spreads, the land will be cursed for them. Freedom is tied to righteousness.

f.g: Set apart, dedicated for a holy purpose.

n: For now it is wise to keep the land hidden from other nations, or they would overrun it and leave no room for Lehi’s descendants.

f.w: kept as yet from the knowledge of other nations

n: Lehi’s covenant promise: if those God brings from Jerusalem keep His commandments, they will prosper, be protected from other nations, and live safely forever.

But if they reject Christ after receiving so much — knowledge of creation, God’s works, power through faith, all the commandments, a choice land — then justice will fall on them. Greater light brings greater accountability.

f.w: the true Messiah, their Redeemer and their God

n: God will bring other nations against them, take away their lands, and scatter them — prophecies fulfilled when the Nephites fell and Lehi’s remaining descendants suffered at the hands of later nations.

f.w: he will bring other nations unto them

n: Generations will see bloodshed and divine judgments. Lehi pleads with his sons to remember and listen.
Lehi’s emotional plea: wake up from the deep sleep of hell and shake off the awful chains of sin that drag people down to misery. Sin is pictured as both sleep and slavery.

Lehi calls himself a “trembling parent” who will soon be buried in the grave, “from whence no traveler can return” — wording similar to a line in Shakespeare’s Hamlet. He is about to go “the way of all the earth,” meaning death.

f.w: the way of all the earth

n: Even facing death, Lehi testifies with joy: the Lord has redeemed his soul, he has seen His glory, and he is eternally encircled in the arms of His love.

f.w: encircled about eternally in the arms of his love

n: His lifelong concern has been that his children keep the Lord’s statutes and judgments.
Lehi has often been heavy with sorrow, afraid that his sons’ hard hearts will bring God’s full wrath and destruction on them.
He also fears a curse lasting many generations — war, famine, hatred, and captivity to the devil.
Lehi wishes they could be a choice and favored people. Yet he submits: God’s will be done, for His ways are always right.
Lehi repeats the core promise of the Book of Mormon: keep the commandments and prosper; disobey and be cut off from God’s presence.

f.w: Inasmuch as ye shall keep my commandments ye shall prosper in the land

n: So that he can die with joy rather than grief, Lehi urges his sons to rise up, be men, and be united in one mind and heart.

f.w: one mind and in one heart

n: Unity and obedience would protect them from a severe curse and from God’s just displeasure that could destroy both body and soul.
Lehi gives a series of commands: wake up, put on the armor of righteousness, shake off chains, come out of obscurity, and rise from the dust. Isaiah used similar words calling Zion to awake.
Lehi defends Nephi: he has kept the commandments, been God’s instrument in bringing them to the promised land, and saved them from starving — yet they tried to kill him.

f.w: instrument in the hands of God

n: Lehi fears Nephi will suffer again at their hands. They have accused Nephi of wanting power, but Lehi testifies Nephi sought only God’s glory and their eternal welfare.

f.w: sought power and authority over you

n: They complained that Nephi was blunt and angry. Lehi explains it was the power of God’s word in him — truth that could not be held back as he boldly named their sins.
God’s power had to be with Nephi; it was the Spirit within him, not Nephi himself, that opened his mouth so he could not stay silent.
If Laman, Lemuel, Sam, and Ishmael’s sons will listen to Nephi, they will not perish, and Lehi will give them his “first blessing” — the birthright blessing normally due the eldest son.

f.g: The birthright blessing, traditionally given to the firstborn son.

n: But if they refuse, Lehi will take the first blessing away and give it to Nephi — echoing how leadership passed from Reuben to Joseph in Israel’s history.
Lehi now addresses Zoram, once Laban’s servant, who joined the family on the way out of Jerusalem. Lehi calls him Nephi’s true friend forever.
Because Zoram has been faithful, his descendants will prosper alongside Nephi’s in the land, and only their own wickedness can disturb that. The Zoramites appear later in Nephite history.

f.w: thy seed shall be blessed with his seed

n: If Zoram’s descendants keep the commandments, the Lord has consecrated the land for their security together with Nephi’s descendants.
